\begin{enumerate}[resume]
\item A card is dealt from a well-shuffled, standard deck of $52$ cards.
Find the probability of being dealt each of the following (write your
answer as a fraction).\begin{multicols}{2}

\begin{enumerate}
\item an ace

\begin{enumerate}
\item []$p(A)=\nicefrac{4}{52}=\nicefrac{1}{13}$\yspace
\end{enumerate}
\item the ace of spades

\begin{enumerate}
\item []$p(A\cap\spadesuit)=\nicefrac{1}{52}$\yspace
\end{enumerate}
\item an ace or a spade

\begin{enumerate}
\item []$p(A\cup\spadesuit)=\nicefrac{4+13-1}{52}=\nicefrac{16}{52}=\nicefrac{4}{13}$\yspace
\end{enumerate}
\item A four of spades

\begin{enumerate}
\item []$p(4\cap\spadesuit)=\nicefrac{4}{52}=\nicefrac{1}{13}$\yspace
\end{enumerate}
\end{enumerate}
\end{multicols}\vfill

\item the probability of getting a head AND rolling a three. 

\begin{enumerate}
\item []$p(H\cap3)=\nicefrac{1}{12}$\yspace
\end{enumerate}
\item {[}2 points{]} the odds of getting a head AND rolling a three.

\begin{enumerate}
\item []$o(H\cap3)=1:11$\yspace
\end{enumerate}
\item the probability of getting a head OR rolling a three.

\begin{enumerate}
\item []$p(H\cup3)=\nicefrac{2+6-1}{12}=\nicefrac{7}{12}$\yspace
\end{enumerate}
\item {[}2 points{]} the odds of getting a head OR rolling a three. 

\begin{enumerate}
\item []$o(H\cup3)=7:5$\yspace
\end{enumerate}

\item {[}6 points each{]} Complete the following:

\begin{enumerate}
\item The MHU librarian has found that the number of books checked out by
students is as follows:

\begin{enumerate}
\item []%
\begin{tabular}{|c|c|c|c|c|}
\hline 
\textbf{Number of Books} & 0 & 1 & 2 & 3\tabularnewline
\hline 
\textbf{proportion} & 25\% & 50\% & 15\% & 10\%\tabularnewline
\hline 
\end{tabular}
\end{enumerate}
Find the expected number of books checked out by a student.

[]$EV=0\cdot.25+1\cdot.50+2\cdot.15+3\cdot.10=1.1$\yspace
\item You have been asked to play a game with a six-sided die. The rules
are as follows.

\begin{itemize}
\item If you roll a 1 or 2 you win \$50.
\item If you roll a 3 you lose \$10.
\item If you roll a 4, 5, or 6 you lose \$20
\end{itemize}
Find the expected value of the game. 
\begin{itemize}
\item []$\nicefrac{2}{6}\cdot50+\nicefrac{1}{6}\cdot(-10)+\nicefrac{3}{6}\cdot(-20)=5$\yspace\vfill
\end{itemize}
\end{enumerate}

While 40\% of the used cars are Fords and the rest are Hondas.\begin{multicols}{2}

\item find the probability that a new car is a Ford.

\begin{enumerate}
\item []$p(N\mid F)=.75$\yspace
\end{enumerate}
\item find the probability that a used car is a Ford.

\begin{enumerate}
\item []$p(U\cap F)=.40\cdot.60=.24$\yspace
\end{enumerate}
\item find the probability that a car on the lot is a Ford. 

\begin{enumerate}
\item []$p(\left(U\cap F\right)\cup\left(N\cap F\right))$\\
\hspace{0cm}\hphantom{$ffffff$}$=.40\cdot.60+.66\cdot.75=.735$\yspace\vspace{-.6cm}
\end{enumerate}
\end{enumerate}
\end{multicols}\vfill\newpage
\item Below are the results of a Gallup poll in which workers were asked
``Would you prefer a male or female boss?''

\begin{tabular}{|c|c|c|c|}
\hline 
 & \textbf{Prefer Male boss} & \textbf{Prefer Female boss} & \textbf{No preference}\tabularnewline
\hline 
Male & 29\% & 18\% & 51\%\tabularnewline
\hline 
Female & 40\% & 27\% & 32\%\tabularnewline
\hline 
\end{tabular}
\begin{enumerate}
\item What is the probability that a worker prefers a female boss?

\begin{enumerate}
\item []$p(PF)=\frac{.18+.27}{2.0}=.225$\yspace
\end{enumerate}
\item What is the probability that a worker prefers a male boss given that
they are female?

\begin{enumerate}
\item []$p(PM\mid F)=.40$\yspace
\end{enumerate}
\item What is the probability that someone is female given that they prefer
a male boss?

\begin{enumerate}
\item []$p(F\mid PM)=\frac{.40}{.29+.40}\approx.58$\yspace
\end{enumerate}
\end{enumerate}
\vfill
\item Of the students who are Biology majors, 55\% are taking Math, 65\%
are taking Art, and 30\% are taking both courses. Find the probability
of the following:\begin{multicols}{2}

\begin{enumerate}
\item a biology major is not taking Math

\begin{enumerate}
\item []$1-.55=.45$\yspace
\end{enumerate}
\item a biology major is taking Math or Art

\begin{enumerate}
\item []$.55+.65-.30=.90$\yspace
\end{enumerate}
\item a biology major is not taking Math and not taking Art. 

\begin{enumerate}
\item []$1-.90=.10$\yspace\columnbreak
\end{enumerate}
\end{enumerate}

\item A die is rolled. The probability of rolling a 5 is $\nicefrac{1}{6}$,
and the probability of rolling a 5 given that a 4 or higher is rolled
is $\nicefrac{1}{3}$.\\
The probability of rolling a 4 or 5 is $\nicefrac{2}{6}=\nicefrac{1}{3}$,
and the probability of rolling a 4 or 5 given that an even number
is rolled is $\nicefrac{1}{3}$. Justify your answers.

\begin{enumerate}
\item Are the events ``rolling a 5'' and ``rolling a 4 or higher'' independent
or dependent?

\begin{enumerate}
\item []Dependent: $p(5)=\nicefrac{1}{6}\neq\nicefrac{1}{3}=p(5\mid4\cup5\cup6)$\yspace
\end{enumerate}
\item Are the events ``rolling a 5'' and ``rolling a 4 or higher'' mutually
exclusive or non-mutually exclusive? 

\begin{enumerate}
\item []Non-mutually exclusive: if you roll a $5$ you also roll a $4$
or higher.\yspace
\end{enumerate}
\item Are the events ``rolling a 5'' and ``rolling an even number''
mutually exclusive or non-mutually exclusive? 

\begin{enumerate}
\item []Mutually exclusive: $5\notin\{2,4,6\}$\yspace
\end{enumerate}
\item Are the events ``rolling a 4 or 5'' and ``rolling an even number''
independent or dependent?

\begin{enumerate}
\item []Independent: $p(4\cup5)=\nicefrac{1}{3}=p(4\cup5\mid2\cup4\cup6)$\yspace\vfill
\end{enumerate}
\end{enumerate}
\item {[}6 points each{]} A jar contains 30 jellybeans. $12$ are red and
$18$ are blue. Jane randomly picks $5$ jellybeans. Find the probability
of each of the following. \textbf{You only need to write the formulas.}
\begin{multicols}{2}

\begin{enumerate}
\item all $5$ are blue.

\begin{enumerate}
\item []$\dfrac{_{18}C_{5}}{_{30}C_{5}}$\yspace
\end{enumerate}
\item exactly $4$ are blue.

\begin{enumerate}
\item []$\dfrac{_{18}C_{4}\times_{12}C_{1}}{_{30}C_{5}}$\yspace\columnbreak
\end{enumerate}
\item $2$ red and $3$ blue. 

\begin{enumerate}
\item []$\dfrac{_{12}C_{2}\cdot_{18}C_{3}}{_{30}C_{5}}$\yspace
\end{enumerate}
\item at least $4$ are blue.

\begin{enumerate}
\item []$\dfrac{_{18}C_{4}\times_{12}C_{1}+{}_{18}C_{5}\times_{12}C_{0}}{_{30}C_{5}}$\yspace\yspace
\end{enumerate}
\end{enumerate}
\end{multicols}\vfill
\end{enumerate}
